correctness.rationale: Theorem 2.3(c) of the directly read Bayer et al. article supplies every exact facet inequality. Averaging size-k ball containment constraints yields \((k+\sqrt{k})\rho\le R_k\); the ball centered at \((1+r)\mathbf1\) attains the minimum of all bounds. An active equality plus all \(n\) lower coordinate bounds forces every center coordinate uniquely. Tangency positions follow from facet normal lengths; the only redundant upper size is never a minimizer. Strict concavity of \(g(t)=t+\sqrt t\), a sufficiently small kinked perturbation and rational/integer scaling prove every k uniquely minimizing for some valid integer parameter vector. The Python reproducer passed 1711 checks, including 80 independent SciPy LP comparisons; these finite tests are corroborative, not universal proof.
